title: Targeting ACOT1-SLC25A5 Axis attenuates LPS-induced acute liver injury by inhibiting ferroptosis and inflammatory responses.
authors: Xu, Chengzhu; Wang, Shun; Wang, Xiyang; Zhang, Xuan; Ouyang, Suxia; Huang, Tingxuan; Jin, Danqun; Zhang, Le; Xu, Yuanyuan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究ACOT1-SLC25A5轴在LPS诱导肝损伤中抑制铁死亡和炎症的机制，虽涉及蛋白互作但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，仅用Rosetta评分辅助验证，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sepsis associated acute liver injury is a major contributor to multiple organ dysfunction and mortality in critically ill patients. ACOT1 has emerged as a promising therapeutic target, demonstrated to inhibit disseminated intravascular coagulation through its anti-ferroptosis activity. However, its specific function and mechanistic role in the context of during endotoxemia-induced liver injury have not been elucidated. This study demonstrates that ferroptosis was markedly activated in both lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated AML12 hepatocytes and LPS-induced acute liver injury mouse models. RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analyses identified ACOT1 as the most significantly downregulated genes following LPS stimulation. Functionally, ACOT1 overexpression upregulated GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression, reduced mitochondrial ROS and Fe(2+) accumulation, which ultimately attenuated LPS-induced hepatocyte ferroptosis. Mechanistically, ACOT1 overexpression activated PPARgamma, thus suppressing NF-kappaB pathway activation and inflammatory responses thereafter. IP-MS and immunofluorescence staining confirmed that SLC25A5 interacts with ACOT1 and functions as a molecular partner in regulating hepatocyte ferroptosis by reducing mitochondrial ROS and Fe(2+) levels. Protein interaction analysis between ACOT1 and SLC25A5 showed a Rosetta score of -271.16 kcal/mol, indicating strong binding affinity. Collectively, our results identified ACOT1 as a novel inhibitor of ferroptosis in LPS-induced acute liver injury. ACOT1 exerts protective effects by modulating the PPARgamma/NF-kappaB signaling axis and cooperating with SLC25A5 to regulate oxidative stress-driven ferroptosis. These results highlight ACOT1 as a potential regulator for inflammatory liver injury.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症相关急性肝损伤是危重症患者多器官功能障碍和死亡的主要原因。ACOT1已被证明是一种有前景的治疗靶点，通过其抗铁死亡活性抑制弥散性血管内凝血。然而，其在内毒素血症诱导的肝损伤中的具体功能和机制作用尚未阐明。本研究表明，在脂多糖（LPS）刺激的AML12肝细胞和LPS诱导的急性肝损伤小鼠模型中，铁死亡均显著激活。RNA测序和生物信息学分析将ACOT1鉴定为LPS刺激后下调最显著的基因之一。功能上，ACOT1过表达上调GPX4和SLC7A11表达，减少线粒体ROS和Fe(2+)积累，最终减轻LPS诱导的肝细胞铁死亡。机制上，ACOT1过表达激活PPARgamma，从而抑制NF-kappaB通路激活及随后的炎症反应。IP-MS和免疫荧光染色证实SLC25A5与ACOT1相互作用，并通过降低线粒体ROS和Fe(2+)水平作为调节肝细胞铁死亡的分子伴侣。ACOT1与SLC25A5之间的蛋白相互作用分析显示Rosetta评分为-271.16 kcal/mol，表明结合亲和力强。总体而言，我们的结果将ACOT1鉴定为LPS诱导急性肝损伤中铁死亡的新型抑制剂。ACOT1通过调节PPARgamma/NF-kappaB信号轴并与SLC25A5协同调节氧化应激驱动的铁死亡发挥保护作用。这些结果突显了ACOT1作为炎症性肝损伤潜在调节因子的作用。
